extracted.intended_audience: NIH applicants and the extramural research community, peer reviewers (study section chairs and SROs), and NIH staff
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and update about NIH's implementation of the Simplified Review Framework (SRF) for most competing research project grant (RPG) applications, including actions to ensure consistent application by CSR staff, study section chairs, and scientific review officers (SROs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the Simplified Review Framework (SRF)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has simplified peer review for most research project grants for application due dates of January 25, 2025 or later; initial applications are under review during summer study section meetings within CSR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRF is intended to address complexity of peer review and potential for reputational bias to affect outcomes. Timeline: applies to due dates Jan 25, 2025 or later; initial implementations occurred in summer 2025 study section meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training of CSR staff on updated criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: CSR extensively trained NIH staff on the updated criteria prior to implementation of the SRF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is a necessary preparatory step to ensure consistent interpretation and application of the updated evaluation criteria across staff involved in peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section chairs guide discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: CSR held a webinar for all study section chairs in recognition of their important role in guiding the discussion during review meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study section chairs are expected to lead and shape meeting discussions to align with the SRF; chairs received targeted guidance via webinar to support this role.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRO pre-meeting coordination with reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: In advance of review meetings, CSR scientific review officers (SROs) meet with all their reviewers to ensure consistent implementation of the updated evaluation and scoring of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs' pre-meeting discussions are intended to align reviewers' understanding of the SRF, scoring approach, and application of updated criteria so that evaluations are consistent across reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRO review of reviewer critiques and pre-meeting feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: SROs read reviewer critiques and provide feedback prior to the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By reviewing critiques and giving feedback before the study section convenes, SROs help improve critique quality and consistency and prepare reviewers for discussion aligned with SRF expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated evaluation and scoring of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRF includes updated evaluation and scoring of applications to simplify peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics of the updated evaluation and scoring are referenced as part of SRF implementation; CSR has trained staff and coordinated reviewers to implement these updated scoring practices consistently (no detailed scoring rules provided on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of reviewer resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer resources are publicly available so that the applicant community can better understand how reviewers are evaluating their grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making reviewer resources public is intended to increase transparency for applicants about evaluation expectations and reviewer practices under the SRF; the page points applicants to those resources for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective to reduce reputational bias and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRF was implemented to address the complexity of the peer review process and the potential for reputational bias to affect peer review outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This objective implies reviewers and NIH staff should focus processes and guidance on minimizing reputational influences and simplifying evaluation to emphasize scientific merit; the page frames bias mitigation as a core aim of the SRF.
